items.title: OpenAI withdraws three manuscripts and revises 14 in an update to openai/math
items.summary: The October 7 update to OpenAI’s openai/math repository withdrew three manuscripts after a sign error in “Algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds” invalidated a stabilization-trace cancellation argument and the construction used by two dependent papers. It revised 14 other manuscripts, updated 13 more to cite the revisions, and added 6 formalizations and 5 supporting additions; the repository now reports 300 of 719 top-line results (about 42%) formalized.

OpenAI releases 722 manuscripts with AI-generated results on open problems
items.summary: OpenAI published 722 mathematical manuscripts in 372 families in its openai/math repository, with Lean formalizations for part of them; 719 remain after the October 7 update. The repository says they were produced by an internal OpenAI model during evaluations on open research problems (the vast majority of results with an unreleased model and one fixed procedure), that the results are at different stages of verification, and that some unformalized results could have issues. The Association for Human Mathematics criticized the release.

items.summary: OpenAI announced GPT-6.1 Sol, which it describes as offering near-Astra intelligence for coding, computer use, and professional work at one-fifth of Astra's standard API token prices.

items.title: Mathematicians Harness Randomness To Crack a 55-Year-Old Conjecture
items.summary: Quanta reports that a group of young mathematicians used randomness to resolve a 55-year-old conjecture, likely inspired by juggling, after a long period without progress.

Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna
items.summary: OpenAI announced GPT-6 Sol and Luna, which it describes as two models bringing frontier intelligence to everyday work with different trade-offs between capability and cost.

items.title: Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence
items.summary: OpenAI says it is working with an independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence to guide how emerging AI results are reviewed and communicated.

items.title: Mathematicians Build Long-Awaited Graph Sandwich
items.summary: Quanta reports that researchers proved a decades-old conjecture about graphs, a result described as giving a new way to understand complex networks.

items.title: In August, 25% of math preprints acknowledged AI use, up from 4% in April
items.summary: Acknowledgments of AI use in arXiv math preprints rose from 4% in April 2026 to 25% in August, with 6% crediting AI with a substantial research contribution.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra leads on math benchmarks, but not on software engineering
items.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra tops the Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI) with a score of 166, ahead of Claude Fable 5.1 at 164 and GPT-5.6 Sol at 162. Its Math-ECI of 170 sets a new record, but on software engineering benchmarks its SWE-ECI of 164 still lags behind Fable 5.1's 167.

items.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking
A human set a new mathematical record. Then AI came for it
items.summary: OpenAI is at the center of another controversy over machines tackling big math problems. This one’s about the twin prime conjecture.

items.title: ZGCM-1 publishes an open training recipe for math and search
items.summary: Researchers introduced a 7B-parameter model aimed at mathematical reasoning and tool-assisted search, alongside weights and training artifacts. The arXiv preprint reports benchmark comparisons based on the authors’ evaluations.

items.title: Clay responds to the announced Navier–Stokes proof
items.summary: Clay acknowledged the announcement of an apparent resolution of the Navier–Stokes problem and said it would follow its published process for evaluating the achievement and assigning credit. The linked OpenAI announcement states a smooth-forced breakdown result.

items.title: A new four-color proof supports faster planar-graph coloring
items.summary: Quanta reports on a 2026 computer-assisted proof that yields near-linear-time four-coloring. The underlying paper was posted in March; September’s article explains the algorithmic advance beyond earlier quadratic-time methods.

items.title: Async GRPO with LoRA across HF Jobs: a bucket, a proxy, and no NCCL
AI may have solved one of math’s biggest puzzles, raising controversy
items.summary: For decades, researchers wondered if the Navier-Stokes equations, which describe fluid flow, break down. OpenAI put thousands of agents on the question.

items.title: Navier–Stokes proof announced; Clay evaluation pending
items.summary: OpenAI released a proposed solution with an analytical write-up and Lean formalization. Clay acknowledged an apparent resolution on September 11 and referred to its evaluation process. The announcement concerns the smooth-forced breakdown alternatives.

items.title: Quanta reports on the announced Navier–Stokes proof
items.summary: Quanta covers OpenAI’s announced smooth-forced Navier–Stokes blowup proof and questions about credit for related work. The report discusses Lean formalization and the need for mathematical scrutiny; Clay’s September 11 response describes its evaluation process.

items.title: OpenAI reports internal measurements of research-agent use
items.summary: OpenAI shared internal measurements of researchers’ agent usage, coding and experiment activity. The report describes rising use and more complex delegated tasks, while noting that compute growth and other bottlenecks limit causal conclusions.

items.title: Live from ICM 2026: What Is Math For in the Age of AI?
items.summary: In this special live recording from the International Congress of Mathematicians in Philadelphia, July 2026, the central question discussed was what do mathematicians really value about doing mathematics in the first place?

items.title: GPT-6 Astra starts its rollout
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Astra for coding, scientific reasoning and computer use. Its announcement reports mathematical results and research benchmarks, with staged availability across ChatGPT and the API.

Gemini 3.8 Flash adds stronger reasoning and coding
items.summary: Google introduced Gemini 3.8 Flash with reported improvements in reasoning, coding and extended tool use. A separate Flash Cyber version is intended for trusted cybersecurity defenders.

items.title: September 2026 update for the 21st edition
Anthropic introduces Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1
items.summary: Anthropic announced two deployments of the same underlying model with different safeguards and access. The company reports improvements in long-running coding and scientific reasoning; Fable is generally available, while Mythos uses a restricted access program.

items.title: Announcing FrontierMath Erdős
items.summary: A benchmark of 68 significant Erdős problems, open as of August 2026, curated by Thomas Bloom and formalized in Lean. AI systems must prove or disprove them within a fixed budget.

items.title: Introducing Gemini 3.7 Flash
MindTopo tests whether AI can preserve topological relationships
items.summary: Microsoft Research introduced a benchmark for reasoning about connectivity, enclosure and related spatial properties. Its tests distinguish recognizing a static diagram from planning changes that preserve topology, where evaluated models showed greater difficulty.

items.title: Ten reported advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science
items.summary: OpenAI published ten results it says resolve or advance longstanding problems, with a paper and reasoning walkthroughs. The announcement covers mathematics and theoretical computer science; each result has its own precise statement and supporting argument.

items.title: 2026 Fields Medals recognize advances across mathematics
items.summary: Clay congratulated John Pardon, Yu Deng, Hong Wang and Jacob Tsimerman on their Fields Medals. The awards recognize contributions spanning geometry and topology, partial differential equations, harmonic analysis and arithmetic geometry.

items.title: Introducing Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber
items.summary: We’re introducing new Gemini models, including Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite and 3.5 Flash Cyber.

items.title: Frontiers of Science Prize
items.summary: The Clay Mathematics Institute congratulated several former Clay Research Fellows, including Terence Tao and James Maynard, and CMI president Martin Bridson on receiving 2026 Frontiers of Science Prizes.

items.title: Introducing Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber
items.summary: Google introduces Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber, a lightweight cybersecurity model to find and patch vulnerabilities.
